simplicity-r1-f1.rationale: The triple-flag pattern is the Gate 2 simplicity-r1-f1 push-back outcome — Round 3 of Gate 2 accepted that `elevation_offered`, `elevation_fired_by`, `elevation_outcome` carry distinct semantic content (offered-vs-fired-vs-outcome), each independently consumed by the eventual `/insights` cadence. The Gate 5 finding's option (a) (add a one-line cross-reference to the `/insights` consumer schema) misframes the calibration: the consumer schema does not yet exist (Phase 3 future skill per PRD line 36-37 + see-also line 191), so cross-referencing to it would create a forward-binding to an unwritten artefact (the same shape Gate 5 surgical-r1-f1 flags). The two-flag collapse in option (b) was already debated and rejected at Gate 2. The Gate 5 finding's underlying observation (~30 lines of bookkeeping) is true but defensible — the bookkeeping is the schema-stability surface for a Phase 3 corpus consumer. Concrete defence: SKILL.md:190-196 (Phase D.3) explicitly documents 'each carries distinct semantic content (offered-vs-fired-vs-outcome), needed for /insights-cadence pattern detection. Collapsing to a single flag would lose signal.' That sentence IS the documentation the finding asks for — the reader can verify the third flag earns its keep against the documented Phase 3 consumer rationale, not against a forward-binding to an unwritten schema. Push-back: the SKILL body already documents the triple-flag earnings; no further change.
